comments.author: aunty_helen
comments.story_title: How a car works (2012)
comments.why_zh: 用更简单的老技术来讲解核心概念的例子。
comments.text_zh: 这很棒。至于说很多内容太老的批评，其实大多数核心概念用更老的技术反而能讲得更好，因为它更简单。这样你就能专注于正在发生什么，而把某个部件或工艺用的是什么技术这类额外细节留到具体案例里再谈。[VIDEO] 就是个很好的例子。话虽如此，写一篇关于 direct injection、common rail 柴油机、高效 turbo charging、variable valve timing、MAF 与 MAP 式 EFI 的文章也值得考虑。
comments.text: This is great. As for the criticism that a lot of the content is old, most of the core concepts can be explained better with older tech as it's simpler. This allows you to focus on what is happening and leave the extra details about what technology a part or process has for a case by case basis. [VIDEO] is a great example of this. Saying that, an article on direct injection, common rail diesels, efficient turbo charging, variable valve timing, MAF VS MAP EFI would be worth considering.

comments.author: japhyr
comments.story_title: 4WD vs. AWD. What's the Difference?
comments.why_zh: 展示了为什么需要 differentials 以及它们如何工作。
comments.quote_zh: 还有一个很棒的 1937 年（！）视频，展示了我们为什么需要 differentials，以及它们是怎么工作的。
comments.text_zh: 对我来说，关键的收获有这些：“多亏了车轴之间的那个 differential，AWD 车会把发动机的动力送到阻力最小的路径上——也就是抓地力最小的那个车轮。两驱车只能在两个车轮之间做选择，而 AWD 系统会在全部四个车轮之间寻找阻力最小的那个。” “4WD 的工作原理是把前轴和后轴锁在一起，在两者之间按 50:50 分配扭矩。这能提供很好的抓地力，但锁在 4WD 模式下的车辆不能在干燥路面上安全行驶，因为它的前轴和后轴被迫以相同的速度转动。” 我记得买第一辆 4wd 车——一辆 '91 年的 Toyota pickup——时还挺害怕的。我知道在干燥路面上不该把车轮锁在 4wd 里，也担心从雪路开到干路面时该怎么办。后来换了 Outback（AWD，不是 4wd），我还在想为什么就不用担心从湿滑路面过渡到干路面了。现在我明白了。还有一个很棒的 1937 年（！）视频，讲的是我们为什么需要 differentials，以及它们是怎么工作的。如果你打算跳过文章，这里是视频的直接链接：[VIDEO]
comments.text: Here are the key takeaways for me: "Thanks to that differential between your axles, an AWD car will send your engine’s power down the path of least resistance—the wheel with the least grip. Where a two-wheel drive car can only choose between two wheels, an AWD system looks for that least resistance across all four wheels." "4WD works by locking the front and rear axles together, splitting torque 50:50 between them. This provides great traction, but a vehicle locked in 4WD cannot safely be operated on dry pavement because its front and rear axles are forced to rotate at the same speeds." I remember being scared when I bought my first 4wd vehicle, a '91 Toyota pickup. I knew I shouldn't have the wheels locked in 4wd on dry pavement, and I was worried about going from snowy roads to dry pavement. When I moved on to an Outback (AWD, not 4wd) I wondered why I didn't have to worry about transitioning between slippery roads and dry pavement. Now I understand. There's also a great video from 1937(!) that shows why we need differentials, and how they work. Here's a direct link to the video if you're going to skip the article: [VIDEO]

comments.author: ironmagma
comments.story_title: Ask HN: What practical skills do you recommend?
comments.why_zh: 学习汽车部件如何工作的起点。
comments.quote_zh: 我可能会从各个单独的部件开始。差速器是如何工作的
comments.text_zh: 我可能会从各个单独的部件开始。差速器是如何工作的：[VIDEO] 关于透明发动机的视频有不少：[LINK] 但如果这不管用，在 YouTube 上搜“how an engine works”应该能找到很多内容。一旦你弄明白发动机如何带动飞轮，你就可以研究飞轮如何通过变速箱把不同的转速施加到车轮上。手动变速箱更简单，所以我会从那里开始：[LINK] 然后再搞清楚离合器在其中起什么作用。之后，你可以接着看液力变矩器（在我看来是最酷的部件，基本上就是一个液力耦合器）和自动变速箱，后者可能会让人脑洞大开。欢迎通过 pc.peterso at Mail of g dot common TLD 联系我，我很乐意分享我学到的东西，帮你省点时间。最后，Engineering Explained 和 howacarworks.com 上有大量小知识，不过后者讲得远比你需要的详细。
comments.text: I would maybe start with the individual components. How a differential works: [VIDEO] There are a number of videos of transparent engines: [LINK] But if that doesn’t work, searching YouTube for “how an engine works” should give lots of content. Once you’ve figured out how the engine turns the flywheel, you can investigate how the flywheel applies different speeds to the wheels via a transmission. Manual transmissions are simpler, so I would start there: [LINK] then figure out how the clutch fits in. After that, you can move on to torque converters (coolest component imo, basically a fluid coupling) and automatic transmissions, which can be a mind-bender. Feel free to reach out to me at pc.peterso at Mail of g dot common TLD, happy to share what I learned and save you some time. Lastly, there is a wealth of tidbits on Engineering Explained and howacarworks.com, although the latter goes into far more detail than you probably need.
